findings.F1: When a coin's 20-day return is negative, the deeper that fall measured in units of its 20-day volatility, the more the coin beats its drift over the next 3 days: the slope of the excess return (in usual moves) on the fall's depth is -0.132 (t -2.23, 5085 non-overlapping cases on 702 days), and at 7 days it is -0.143 (t -2.01, 2162 cases on 299 days). After 20-day rises the slope is +0.051 (t 1.60), a different shape.
findings.F2: The rebound after deeper 20-day falls holds across most years. At 3 days the depth slope is positive in 6 of 8 years: 2019 and 2021–2025, from 0.084 to 0.263, and 2025 alone has t 2.69. At 7 days, leaving out 2022, the slope is 0.163 (t 2.01, 1793 cases on 253 days).

ideas.idea: The deeper a coin's 20-day fall, measured against its own daily volatility over those 20 days, the more the coin rises above its usual drift over the next 3 to 7 days.
ideas.consequence: A coin sharply oversold over 20 days relative to its own volatility is a reason to buy for a rebound of a few days, and a reason not to short it.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled 20-day fall rebound

ideas.idea: The longer a coin's 5-day return has stayed positive day after day, the more the coin rises above its usual drift over the next 7 days.
ideas.consequence: A rise that has persisted for many days is a reason to keep holding the coin for a week rather than exit after a few days.
ideas.name: persistent rise keeps rising
